# A Session schema for the agents sidebar

- Status: planned
- Links: [research](../../docs/research/agent-session-261020.md) · PR #18 (the agents sidebar) · PR #20 (Session in the glossary) · [icebox: the sign-in session table](auth-session-name.md) · branch `docs/session-schema-plan`

The agents sidebar keeps each row's state, task kind, title and nesting in the web app alone. `AgentState` and `AgentTask` are the keys of `stateIcons` and `taskIcons` in `web/next/src/components/agents/icons.ts`, and `title` and `subagents` sit on the row types in `agents/sidebar.tsx`. All four describe one run of an agent, which the glossary calls a Session, so they move into a `Session` schema in `packages/schema`, beside `Agent`. A subagent's run becomes a child session that points at the session that started it, as OpenCode, Codex and eve model it.

## Decided

1. **The field's name is `status`** (2026-10-20), the name seven of the nine sources use, so the icons page's State section becomes Status.
2. **All nine values stay** (2026-10-20): cancelled, completed, failed, idle, paused, pending, running, stuck and waiting. Sessions run as CLIs in herdr panes, where a rate limit pauses a session and an unrecognized screen can leave it stuck, so each value has a way to be detected: herdr's own status (`working`, `blocked`, `idle`), the harness's hooks (a `StopFailure` with `rate_limit`) and its wording on screen, or the server (a session that stopped making progress).
3. **Stuck and waiting stay apart** (2026-10-20). Waiting: the agent asked the human something on purpose, a question or a permission, which the UI can answer. Stuck: the agent is not moving and asked nothing the server understands, such as an unrecognized screen or one that has not changed for a long time, so a person has to look at the pane.
4. **A reason and an until time beside the status** (2026-10-20): `reason`, a short text such as "rate limit" or "permission for npm test", and `until`, a time used only while paused, so the UI can count down and the server knows when to check again. On the CLI route `until` comes from the reset time Claude Code passes to a status-line command (`rate_limits.*.resets_at`), since the time on screen has no date and is not parsed. Claude Code's `waitingFor`, OpenCode's retry message and next time, and Cloudflare's interrupted reason do the same.
5. **An optional task kind on the session** (2026-10-20), one of the thirteen on `/docs/ui/icons`, set by whoever starts the session, usually an orchestrator starting a subagent (`zerosdk session start --agent builder --task debug`), since the glossary defines a subagent as started for one task, so the same agent can build one day and debug the next. No source has such a field; it is ZeroSDK's own, and a session started without one shows its status icon.
6. **A session names its agent by `Id`** (2026-10-20), as `fallbacks` already references agents, so renaming an agent never breaks its sessions; the UI shows the name by looking the `Id` up, and the server does the same when it launches Claude with `--agent`. Seven of the nine sources reference by name; OpenCode references by id.
7. **A session keeps its parent and its root** (2026-10-20). The server writes both when it opens the session: `parent`, the session that asked for it, and `root`, the top of its tree, so the permission flipper finds a session's main agent in one look on every request, as eve's `rootSessionId` does. Depth is worked out when a session starts, from the short chain, and is not stored.
8. **Title, ticket and pull request are three fields** (2026-10-20): `ticket` (such as `ZS-12`, set at start), `pullRequest` (a number, filled in once the agent opens one) and `title` (set at start, renamable), all optional; the row composes `ZS-12#45 Add tools` and can link the ticket and the pull request, as Claude Code's agent view shows a pull request label beside a session's name.

## Steps

1. Add `packages/schema/src/session.ts` on the conventions `Agent` follows (Zod 4, keys A to Z, `Id` from `common.ts`, a JSDoc description per field drafted from the sources' own wording), show it to the user before anything uses it, and record its shape in an ADR. Add a Session reference page after Agent, with the sources' session types generated by a script, as `bun run agent:schemas` generates Agent's.
2. Key `stateIcons` and `taskIcons` by the schema's values, the way `effortIcons` is keyed by `Agent["effort"]`, and rename the icons page's State section to Status.
3. Make each sidebar row an `Agent` and its `Session`, build the nesting from the parent field, and fold `AgentRow`, `SubagentRow` and `NestedSubagentRow` into one row type.
4. Settle the [icebox: the sign-in session table](auth-session-name.md) when the sessions table is designed, since agent sessions then get a table beside the sign-in `session` table.
5. Update the tests under `tests/web/next/src/components/agents/`, the `/docs/ui/sidebar` page and the `design` and `codebase-map` skills, and check the sidebar in a real browser.
